questions.text: Which economic concept refers to the next-best alternative forgone?
questions.explanation: Because resources are limited, every choice means giving something up. The value of the next-best option you forgo is the opportunity cost - the course's central concept (theory Q3: the forgone ₦3,000 job is the cost of studying).

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO101_practice_test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: A point inside a Production Possibility Frontier indicates:
questions.explanation: Points ON the frontier use all resources efficiently. A point inside means some resources are idle or misallocated, so the economy could produce more of both goods without any new resources. A point outside is unattainable with current resources and technology.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO101_practice_test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: According to the law of demand, when price rises, quantity demanded generally:
questions.explanation: Price and quantity demanded are inversely related (ceteris paribus). As price rises, consumers buy less and substitute toward cheaper alternatives; as price falls, they buy more.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO101_practice_test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which factor causes a movement along the demand curve?
opts: A change in the good's own price
A change in the number of buyers
questions.explanation: Only the good's own price moves you along a given demand curve. Income, tastes, expectations, related prices and buyer numbers are non-price determinants - they shift the entire curve (theory Q7).

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO101_practice_test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: When market price is above equilibrium, the market normally experiences:
questions.explanation: At a price above equilibrium, sellers offer more than buyers want: quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded, creating a surplus. Unsold stock then puts downward pressure on price toward equilibrium (theory Q9).

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO101_practice_test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: If price elasticity of demand is 0.5, demand is:
questions.explanation: The course classifies by magnitude: |Ed| < 1 is inelastic - quantity demanded responds proportionately LESS than price (typical of necessities). |Ed| > 1 is elastic; Ed = 1 is unitary.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO101_practice_test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Cross-price elasticity of demand for two substitute goods is generally:
questions.explanation: For substitutes (tea vs coffee), a price rise in one pushes consumers toward the other, so the quantity demanded of the second RISES with the first good's price: cross-price elasticity is positive. Complements are negative (theory Q14).

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO101_practice_test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: A binding price ceiling set below equilibrium tends to create:
questions.explanation: A ceiling below equilibrium holds the price artificially low, so buyers demand more than sellers will supply - a shortage, with rationing, reduced production and declining quality among the listed effects (theory Q16).

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO101_practice_test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: In the short run, production is characterised by:
opts: At least one fixed factor of production
questions.explanation: The short run is defined ECONOMICALLY, not by calendar time: at least one factor (typically capital) is fixed while others can be varied. In the long run all factors are variable (theory Q20).

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO101_practice_test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Which market structure has a few dominant, interdependent firms?
questions.explanation: Oligopoly: a small number of large firms dominate, and each firm's pricing/output decisions directly affect rivals, who must react - strategic interdependence (theory Q26).

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO101_practice_test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Firms in perfect competition are described as:
opts: Price makers with complete market control
The only sellers in the market
questions.explanation: With many small sellers of a homogeneous product and free entry/exit, no single firm can influence the market price - each is a price TAKER. Monopoly firms, by contrast, have significant price-setting power (theory Q25).

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO101_practice_test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Marginal product measures:
opts: Additional output from an additional unit of variable input
questions.explanation: MP = ΔTP / ΔL: the extra output produced by adding ONE more unit of the variable input (e.g. the 5th worker adds 42-39 = 3 units), holding other inputs fixed (theory Q22, calculation Q30).

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO101_practice_test (key authored from course content)

questions.text: Economics is best described as the study of:
opts: Scarcity and its implications for the use of resources
questions.explanation: The course defines economics as the study of scarcity and its implications for resource use, production, and societal welfare.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO 101 theory Q1

questions.text: A student spends three hours studying instead of working a job that would pay N3,000. In the course's example, the forgone N3,000 represents:
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the next-best alternative forgone; the guide uses exactly this example.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO 101 theory Q3

questions.text: On a Production Possibility Frontier, a point INSIDE the frontier represents:
questions.explanation: Points on the frontier are efficient; inside means resources are not fully or efficiently used; outside is unattainable.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO 101 theory Q4

questions.text: Equity, as distinguished from efficiency in the course material, concerns:
opts: The fairness of how resources and benefits are distributed
questions.explanation: Efficiency is about maximising output from limited resources; equity concerns fairness of distribution.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO 101 theory Q5

questions.text: A movement ALONG the demand curve is caused by:
opts: A change in the price of the commodity itself
A change in the number of buyers
questions.explanation: Only a change in the good's own price causes movement along the curve; other determinants shift the curve.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO 101 theory Q7

questions.text: Which of the following is listed as a determinant that SHIFTS the supply curve?
questions.explanation: Input prices, technology, expectations and number of sellers shift supply; own price only causes movement along the curve.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO 101 theory Q8

questions.text: The price of a commodity rises by 20% and quantity demanded falls by 40%. Price elasticity of demand is:
questions.explanation: Ed = 40/20 = 2; because the magnitude exceeds one, demand is elastic.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO 101 calculation Q27

questions.text: A binding price ceiling set below equilibrium typically leads to:
opts: A shortage, rationing and reduced quality
questions.explanation: The guide lists shortage, rationing, reduced production, quality decline and inefficiency as effects of a ceiling below equilibrium.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO 101 theory Q16

questions.text: Nigeria's minimum wage policy is given in the course as an example of:
questions.explanation: A price floor is a legal minimum price; the course cites the minimum wage as its example.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO 101 theory Q17

questions.text: A firm records total product of 39 units with 4 workers and 42 units with 5 workers. The marginal product of the fifth worker is:
questions.explanation: MP = change in TP / change in L = (42-39)/(5-4) = 3; the guide also uses this to illustrate diminishing returns.

source.label: MIVA practice questions.pdf - ECO 101 calculation Q30

questions.text: If the price of a good falls and the quantity demanded increases, this is represented by:
opts: A movement along a given demand curve
A shift of the demand curve
A movement of the supply curve
A change in market equilibrium only
questions.explanation: A price change causes movement along the existing demand curve; only non-price determinants shift the curve.

source.label: Economics 103 exam MCQs (BCcampus/eCampusOntario Principles of Microeconomics, OpenStax adaptation)

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a determinant of the demand for good X?
opts: The income of consumers who buy good X
The cost of labour used to produce good X
The price of good Y, a complement to X
The number of buyers of good X
questions.explanation: Input costs are a supply-side factor; demand determinants include income, prices of related goods and number of buyers.

source.label: Economics 103 exam MCQs (BCcampus/eCampusOntario Principles of Microeconomics, OpenStax adaptation)

questions.text: According to marginal analysis, optimal decision-making involves taking actions whenever:
opts: Marginal benefit is positive regardless of cost
questions.explanation: Marginal analysis says expand an activity while marginal benefit exceeds marginal cost.

source.label: Economics 103 exam MCQs (BCcampus/eCampusOntario Principles of Microeconomics, OpenStax adaptation)

questions.text: A decrease in quantity demanded (not a decrease in demand) is graphically represented by:
opts: A leftward shift of the demand curve
A rightward shift of the demand curve
A movement up and to the left along the demand curve
A movement down and to the right along the demand curve
questions.explanation: A higher own-price reduces quantity demanded as a movement up the curve; shifts reflect non-price factors.

source.label: Economics 103 exam MCQs (BCcampus/eCampusOntario Principles of Microeconomics, OpenStax adaptation)

questions.text: If goods X and Y are substitutes, an increase in the price of X will result in:
opts: A decrease in the equilibrium quantity of Y
An increase in the equilibrium quantity of Y
No change in the market for Y
A decrease in demand for Y
questions.explanation: When substitutes are involved, a higher price for X pushes consumers toward Y, raising Y's demand and equilibrium quantity.

source.label: Economics 103 exam MCQs (BCcampus/eCampusOntario Principles of Microeconomics, OpenStax adaptation)

questions.text: If cookies are a normal good and consumer incomes increase, we would expect:
opts: An increase in equilibrium price and quantity
A decrease in equilibrium price and quantity
A decrease in price with an increase in quantity
No change in the cookie market
questions.explanation: Higher income raises demand for a normal good, increasing both equilibrium price and quantity.

source.label: Economics 103 exam MCQs (BCcampus/eCampusOntario Principles of Microeconomics, OpenStax adaptation)
